name: notespace
description: A local-first workspace for VS Code: wiki and docs with a visual Markdown editor, tasks, Kanban boards, calendar, notebooks, dashboards and an API client — all in your files.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: Running notebook cells and code blocks, and sending API Playground requests, require a trusted workspace. Reading, editing, dashboards, search and exporting work without trust.

viewsWelcome.contents:
NoteSpace keeps documentation as local Markdown files.
[Create Wiki](command:wikiStudio.createWiki)
[Import Markdown or MkDocs Project](command:wikiStudio.importProject)
Already have Markdown in a folder named `wiki`? [New Page](command:wikiStudio.newPage) creates the first one.

Open a wiki page to see its outline, backlinks, links and properties here.
Tip: drag this view to the Secondary Side Bar to keep it beside your editor.

Home, tasks, boards and calendar for this wiki.
[Open Home](command:wikiStudio.home)

wikiStudio.root.description: Wiki directory relative to each workspace folder. Use '.' to index the whole folder.

wikiStudio.exclude.description: Glob of files excluded from the wiki index.

wikiStudio.respectGitignore.markdownDescription: Leave out pages that Git ignores (`.gitignore` files of the workspace folder, including nested files and `!` negations). Off by default so private, ignored notes stay visible in your wiki.

enumDescriptions: Studio, or Code when Studio cannot keep the page's Markdown exactly
wikiStudio.openPagesIn.description: Where pages open from the Pages view, search and links.

wikiStudio.explorer.humanizeNames.markdownDescription: Show readable labels in the Pages view for folders and for pages without a title (`getting-started.md` → Getting Started). Page titles from front matter or a `#` heading are shown as written; files are never renamed.

wikiStudio.explorer.acronyms.description: Words kept in this exact casing in readable labels.

wikiStudio.explorer.directorySort.markdownDescription: Order of folders and pages in the Pages view. A folder's `index.md` or `README.md` is always listed first; within groups, `navigation.sort` in wiki.yaml applies.

wikiStudio.explorer.autoReveal.description: Select the active page in the Pages view when you switch editors.

wikiStudio.diagnostics.description: Report broken, ambiguous and missing-heading links.

wikiStudio.maxFileSizeKB.description: Maximum page size to index, in KiB.

wikiStudio.maxPages.description: Maximum pages to index per workspace folder.

wikiStudio.maxIndexSizeMB.description: Maximum total on-disk page content to index per wiki, in MiB.

wikiStudio.editor.width.description: Width of the Studio writing column.

wikiStudio.dailyNotes.folder.description: Folder (relative to the wiki root) that holds one daily note per date, named YYYY-MM-DD.md.

wikiStudio.dailyNotes.template.description: Template page for new daily notes, relative to the wiki root (for example .templates/Daily.md). Supports {{title}}, {{date}}, {{weekday}}, {{yesterday}} and {{tomorrow}}. Empty uses the built-in template.

wikiStudio.api.folder.description: Folder (relative to the first workspace folder) for API collections and environments.

wikiStudio.api.maxResponseMB.description: Responses larger than this are truncated (the rest is not downloaded).

wikiStudio.api.historyLimit.description: How many sent requests the API history keeps (0 keeps none). History stores method, redacted address, status, time and size; never bodies or credentials.

wikiStudio.home.openOnStartup.description: Open the NoteSpace Home when the NoteSpace sidebar opens and no editor is open.

wikiStudio.boards.folder.description: Folder (in the wiki) suggested for new board files.

wikiStudio.notes.folder.description: Folder (in the wiki) for New Note. Empty: the wiki root.

wikiStudio.tasks.captureTo.markdownDescription: Where global quick capture writes new tasks. Tasks created on a board go to the board's file; tasks typed in a page stay in that page.

wikiStudio.planner.timeZone.description: IANA time zone used to decide which day is today (for example Europe/Rome). Empty uses this machine's zone.

wikiStudio.planner.inbox.description: Page (relative to the wiki root) where Quick Add and Add Task write new tasks.

wikiStudio.planner.upcomingDays.description: How many days ahead the Upcoming list shows.

wikiStudio.planner.reminders.description: Show one notification per day for tasks due today or overdue while VS Code is running. No reminders fire while VS Code or code-server is closed.

wikiStudio.notebooks.pythonKernel.description: Offer the NoteSpace Python kernel in the notebook editor when python3 is available. Cells run only when you run them, and only in trusted workspaces.

wikiStudio.codeRunner.enabled.description: Show a Run button on Python, JavaScript and Bash code blocks in Studio. Runs only on click, only in trusted workspaces, after a per-session confirmation for each runtime.

wikiStudio.codeRunner.timeoutSeconds.description: Maximum run time for a code block before it is stopped.

enumDescriptions: Language models available in VS Code (for example from a chat extension). VS Code asks for permission the first time.
An OpenAI-compatible endpoint you configure, such as a local Ollama or llama.cpp server.
wikiStudio.ai.provider.markdownDescription: Where AI commands send text. Every request asks for confirmation and results are proposals you review before applying.

wikiStudio.ai.endpoint.markdownDescription: Base URL of an OpenAI-compatible API (`/chat/completions`, `/embeddings`). Used when `wikiStudio.ai.provider` is `endpoint` and by semantic search.

wikiStudio.ai.model.markdownDescription: Chat model name at the endpoint, for example `llama3.1`.

wikiStudio.semanticSearch.model.markdownDescription: Embedding model at `wikiStudio.ai.endpoint` for **Semantic Search**, for example `nomic-embed-text`. Empty disables semantic search. NoteSpace never downloads models.

wikiStudio.export.browserPath.markdownDescription: Path to a Chromium-based browser (Chrome, Edge, Chromium, Brave) used in headless mode to create PDFs. Empty: detect an installed one. Without a browser, **Export PDF** saves a print-ready HTML page instead.

scripts.test: npm run typecheck && npm run test:unit
scripts.check: npm test && npm run test:integration && npm run package && npm run test:code-server && npm run test:rich && npm run test:planner
scripts.vscode:prepublish: npm run typecheck && npm run build && npm run notices
